sanskrit: jyotiṣaś ca guṇo rūpaṃ cakṣuṣā tac ca gṛhyate cakṣuḥsthaś ca tathādityo rūpajñāne vidhīyate
english: The quality of light is form, and form is grasped by the eye; and the sun, seated within the eye, is ordained for the knowing of form.

sanskrit: vāyavyas tu tathā sparśas tvacā prajñāyate ca saḥ tvaksthaś caiva tathā vāyuḥ sparśajñāne vidhīyate
english: Touch belongs to the wind, and it is perceived by the skin; and the wind, seated within the skin, is ordained for the knowing of touch.

sanskrit: ākāśasya guṇo ghoṣaḥ śrotreṇa sa tu gṛhyate śrotrasthāś ca diśaḥ sarvāḥ śabdajñāne prakīrtitāḥ
english: The quality of ether is sound, and it is grasped by the ear; and all the quarters, seated within the ear, are declared the means for knowing sound.

sanskrit: manasas tu guṇaś cintā prajñayā sa tu gṛhyate hṛdisthacetanādhātur manojñāne vidhīyate
english: The quality of mind is thought, and it is grasped by understanding; and the conscious element seated in the heart is ordained for the knowing of mind.

sanskrit: buddhir adhyavasāyena dhyānena ca mahāṃs tathā niścitya grahaṇaṃ nityam avyaktaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: The intellect acts through resolve, and the Great One through meditation; their grasping is ever a determining—the Unmanifest, in this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: aliṅgagrahaṇo nityaḥ kṣetrajño nirguṇātmakaḥ tasmād aliṅgaḥ kṣetrajñaḥ kevalaṃ jñānalakṣaṇaḥ
english: The Knower of the Field is eternal, grasped by no sign, devoid of qualities in its nature; therefore the Knower of the Field is signless, marked by pure knowledge alone.

sanskrit: avyaktaṃ kṣetram uddiṣṭaṃ guṇānāṃ prabhavāpyayam sadā paśyāmy ahaṃ līnaṃ vijānāmi śṛṇomi ca
english: The Unmanifest is declared the Field, the source and dissolution of the qualities. Ever do I see what lies hidden within; I know it, and I hear it.

sanskrit: puruṣas tad vijānīte tasmāt kṣetrajña ucyate guṇavṛttaṃ tathā kṛtsnaṃ kṣetrajñaḥ paripaśyati
english: The Spirit comes to know that Field, and therefore is called the Knower of the Field; the Knower of the Field beholds the whole working of the qualities entire.

sanskrit: ādimadhyāvasānāntaṃ sṛjyamānam acetanam na guṇā vidur ātmānaṃ sṛjyamānaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
english: With beginning, middle, and end as its limits, unconscious and ever being created—the qualities, themselves created again and again, do not know the Self.

sanskrit: na satyaṃ veda vai kaś cit kṣetrajñas tv eva vindati guṇānāṃ guṇabhūtānāṃ yat paraṃ parato mahat
english: Indeed none knows the truth; the Knower of the Field alone attains that which is higher than the high, greater than the qualities and what is born of them.

sanskrit: tasmād guṇāṃś ca tattvaṃ ca parityajyeha tattvavit kṣīṇadoṣo guṇān hitvā kṣetrajñaṃ praviśaty atha
english: Therefore the knower of truth, abandoning here both the qualities and their principle, with his faults worn away and the qualities forsaken, then enters into the Knower of the Field.

sanskrit: nirdvaṃdvo nirnamaskāro niḥsvadhākāra eva ca acalaś cāniketaś ca kṣetrajñaḥ sa paro vibhuḥ
english: Free from the pairs of opposites, beyond salutation and beyond the offering-cry, unmoving and homeless—that Knower of the Field is the supreme, all-pervading Lord.

sanskrit: brahmovāca yad ādimadhyaparyantaṃ grahaṇopāyam eva ca nāmalakṣaṇasaṃyuktaṃ sarvaṃ vakṣyāmi tattvataḥ
english: Brahmā said: That which has beginning, middle, and end, together with the means of its apprehension, joined with name and mark—all this I shall declare to you in truth.

sanskrit: ahaḥ pūrvaṃ tato rātrir māsāḥ śuklādayaḥ smṛtāḥ śraviṣṭhādīni ṛkṣāṇi ṛtavaḥ śiśirādayaḥ
english: Day comes first, then night; the months are reckoned from the bright fortnight onward; the lunar mansions from Śraviṣṭhā onward, and the seasons from the cool season onward.

sanskrit: bhūmir ādis tu gandhānāṃ rasānām āpa eva ca rūpāṇāṃ jyotir ādis tu sparśādir vāyur ucyate śabdasyādis tathākāśam eṣa bhūtakṛto guṇaḥ
english: Earth is the source of scents, and water of tastes; light is the source of forms, and wind is called the origin of touch; ether is the source of sound—such is the quality wrought by the elements.

sanskrit: ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi bhūtānām ādim uttamam ādityo jyotiṣām ādir agnir bhūtādir iṣyate
english: Beyond this I shall now proclaim the highest origin of beings: the sun is the source of lights, and fire is held to be the source of the elements.

sanskrit: sāvitrī sarvavidyānāṃ devatānāṃ prajāpatiḥ oṃkāraḥ sarvavedānāṃ vacasāṃ prāṇa eva ca yady asmin niyataṃ loke sarvaṃ sāvitram ucyate
english: The Sāvitrī is the source of all branches of knowledge, Prajāpati of the gods; the syllable Oṃ is the source of all the Vedas, and breath of speech; whatever is fixed in this world is all called Sāvitra, born of the Sun.

sanskrit: gāyatrī chandasām ādiḥ paśūnām aja ucyate gāvaś catuṣpadām ādir manuṣyāṇāṃ dvijātayaḥ
english: The Gāyatrī is the source of metres; the goat is called the source of cattle; cows are the source of four-footed beasts, and the twice-born of men.

sanskrit: śyenaḥ patatriṇām ādir yajñānāṃ hutam uttamam parisarpiṇāṃ tu sarveṣāṃ jyeṣṭhaḥ sarpo dvijottamāḥ
english: The hawk is the source of birds, the oblation the highest of sacrifices; and of all creeping things the serpent is the foremost, O best of the twice-born.

sanskrit: kṛtam ādir yugānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ hiraṇyaṃ sarvaratnānām oṣadhīnāṃ yavās tathā
english: The Kṛta is the first of all the ages—in this there is no doubt; gold is the first of all gems, and barley of the healing herbs.

sanskrit: sarveṣāṃ bhakṣyabhojyānām annaṃ paramam ucyate dravāṇāṃ caiva sarveṣāṃ peyānām āpa uttamāḥ
english: Of all things to be chewed and eaten, grain is called supreme; and of all fluids that may be drunk, water is the highest.

sanskrit: sthāvarāṇāṃ ca bhūtānāṃ sarveṣām aviśeṣataḥ brahmakṣetraṃ sadā puṇyaṃ plakṣaḥ prathamajaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: Among all immovable beings without distinction, the ever-holy plakṣa tree, the field of Brahman, is remembered as the first-born.

sanskrit: ahaṃ prajāpatīnāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ mama viṣṇur acintyātmā svayaṃbhūr iti sa smṛtaḥ
english: And I am the first of all the Prajāpatis—in this there is no doubt; Viṣṇu, whose nature is beyond thought, is mine, and he is remembered as the Self-existent.

sanskrit: parvatānāṃ mahāmeruḥ sarveṣām agrajaḥ smṛtaḥ diśāṃ ca pradiśāṃ cordhvā digjātā prathamaṃ tathā
english: The great Meru is remembered as the eldest-born of all the mountains; and of the quarters and intermediate quarters, the upward direction was born first.

sanskrit: tathā tripathagā gaṅgā nadīnām agrajā smṛtā tathā sarodapānānāṃ sarveṣāṃ sāgaro 'grajaḥ
english: So too Gaṅgā, who flows by three paths, is remembered as the eldest-born of rivers; and the ocean is the eldest of all lakes and wells of water.

sanskrit: devadānavabhūtānāṃ piśācoragarakṣasām narakiṃnarayakṣāṇāṃ sarveṣām īśvaraḥ prabhuḥ
english: Of gods, demons, and spirits, of piśācas, serpents, and rākṣasas, of men, kiṃnaras, and yakṣas—of all he is the Lord and ruler.

sanskrit: ādir viśvasya jagato viṣṇur brahmamayo mahān bhūtaṃ parataraṃ tasmāt trailokye neha vidyate
english: Viṣṇu, the mighty one made of Brahman, is the source of the whole universe; no being higher than he exists here in the three worlds.

sanskrit: āśramāṇāṃ ca gārhasthyaṃ sarveṣāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ lokānām ādir avyaktaṃ sarvasyāntas tad eva ca
english: Of all the stages of life, the householder's is the first—in this there is no doubt; the Unmanifest is the source of the worlds, and it too is the end of all.

sanskrit: ahāny astamayāntāni udayāntā ca śarvarī sukhasyāntaḥ sadā duḥkhaṃ duḥkhasyāntaḥ sadā sukham
english: Days end in sunset, and night ends with the rising of the sun; the end of pleasure is ever pain, and the end of pain is ever pleasure.

sanskrit: sarve kṣayāntā nicayāḥ patanāntāḥ samucchrayāḥ saṃyogā viprayogāntā maraṇāntaṃ hi jīvitam
english: All accumulations end in waste, all risings end in a fall; unions end in separation, and life indeed ends in death.

sanskrit: sarvaṃ kṛtaṃ vināśāntaṃ jātasya maraṇaṃ dhruvam aśāśvataṃ hi loke 'smin sarvaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam
english: Everything done ends in destruction; for what is born, death is certain; in this world all things, moving and unmoving, are impermanent.

sanskrit: iṣṭaṃ dattaṃ tapo 'dhītaṃ vratāni niyamāś ca ye sarvam etad vināśāntaṃ jñānasyānto na vidyate
english: Sacrifice offered, gifts given, austerity, study, vows, and observances—all of this ends in destruction; only of knowledge there is no end.

sanskrit: tasmāj jñānena śuddhena prasannātmā samāhitaḥ nirmamo nirahaṃkāro mucyate sarvapāpmabhiḥ
english: Therefore, by pure knowledge, with serene and steadfast self, free from possessiveness and from the sense of 'I,' one is released from all evils.

sanskrit: brahmovāca buddhisāraṃ manastambham indriyagrāmabandhanam mahābhūtāraviṣkambhaṃ nimeṣapariveṣṭanam
english: Brahmā said: With intellect for its core, mind for its pillar, the host of the senses for its fastenings, the great elements for its struts, and the blinking of an eye for its rim—

sanskrit: jarāśokasamāviṣṭaṃ vyādhivyasanasaṃcaram deśakālavicārīdaṃ śramavyāyāmanisvanam
english: beset by old age and grief, coursing with disease and misfortune, ranging over place and time, sounding with toil and exertion—

sanskrit: ahorātraparikṣepaṃ śītoṣṇaparimaṇḍalam sukhaduḥkhāntasaṃkleśaṃ kṣutpipāsāvakīlanam
english: with day and night for its circuit, cold and heat for its circling ring, the torments that end in pleasure and pain, and hunger and thirst for its rivets—

sanskrit: chāyātapavilekhaṃ ca nimeṣonmeṣavihvalam ghoramohajanākīrṇaṃ vartamānam acetanam
english: streaked with shadow and sunlight, tossed by the closing and opening of eyes, thronged with men of dreadful delusion, ever turning, and unconscious—

sanskrit: māsārdhamāsagaṇitaṃ viṣamaṃ lokasaṃcaram tamonicayapaṅkaṃ ca rajovegapravartakam
english: counted by months and half-months, uneven, ranging through the worlds, with the heaped mire of darkness and driven by the rush of passion—

sanskrit: sattvālaṃkāradīptaṃ ca guṇasaṃghātamaṇḍalam svaravigrahanābhīkaṃ śokasaṃghātavartanam
english: bright with the ornament of goodness, a wheel formed of the mass of the qualities, with quarrel and discord for its nave, revolving with massed griefs—

sanskrit: kriyākāraṇasaṃyuktaṃ rāgavistāram āyatam lobhepsāparisaṃkhyātaṃ viviktajñānasaṃbhavam
english: joined with action and its cause, broad with the spread of desire, reckoned by greed and craving, yet the birthplace of discerning knowledge—

sanskrit: bhayamohaparīvāraṃ bhūtasaṃmohakārakam ānandaprītidhāraṃ ca kāmakrodhaparigraham
english: surrounded by fear and delusion, working the bewilderment of beings, bearing within it joy and delight, and the grasp of desire and anger—

sanskrit: mahadādiviśeṣāntam asaktaprabhavāvyayam manojavanam aśrāntaṃ kālacakraṃ pravartate
english: reaching from the Great Principle to the particulars, with unattached origin and undecaying, swift as the mind and tireless—thus the wheel of Time turns onward.

sanskrit: etad dvaṃdvasamāyuktaṃ kālacakram acetanam visṛjet saṃkṣipec cāpi bodhayet sāmaraṃ jagat
english: This wheel of Time, yoked with the pairs of opposites and unconscious, may send forth the world together with its gods, draw it back, and awaken it.

sanskrit: kālacakrapravṛttiṃ ca nivṛttiṃ caiva tattvataḥ yas tu veda naro nityaṃ na sa bhūteṣu muhyati
english: But the man who truly and ever knows the turning forth and the turning back of the wheel of Time is not bewildered among created beings.

sanskrit: vimuktaḥ sarvasaṃkleśaiḥ sarvadvaṃdvātigo muniḥ vimuktaḥ sarvapāpebhyaḥ prāpnoti paramāṃ gatim
english: Freed from all torments, the sage who has passed beyond all pairs of opposites, released from all sins, attains the supreme goal.

sanskrit: gṛhastho brahmacārī ca vānaprastho 'tha bhikṣukaḥ catvāra āśramāḥ proktāḥ sarve gārhasthyamūlakāḥ
english: The householder, the celibate student, the forest-dweller, and the mendicant—these four stages of life are declared, all of them rooted in the householder's state.

sanskrit: yaḥ kaś cid iha loke ca hy āgamaḥ saṃprakīrtitaḥ tasyāntagamanaṃ śreyaḥ kīrtir eṣā sanātanī
english: Whatever scripture is proclaimed here in this world, to reach its end is the higher good—this is the eternal renown.

sanskrit: saṃskāraiḥ saṃskṛtaḥ pūrvaṃ yathāvac caritavrataḥ jātau guṇaviśiṣṭāyāṃ samāvarteta vedavit
english: First consecrated by the sacraments, having duly fulfilled his vows, born in a family distinguished by virtue, the knower of the Veda should return home from his studentship.

sanskrit: svadāranirato dāntaḥ śiṣṭācāro jitendriyaḥ pañcabhiś ca mahāyajñaiḥ śraddadhāno yajeta ha
english: Devoted to his own wife, self-controlled, of cultivated conduct, with senses subdued, full of faith, he should worship with the five great sacrifices.

sanskrit: devatātithiśiṣṭāśī nirato vedakarmasu ijyāpradānayuktaś ca yathāśakti yathāvidhi
english: Eating what remains after the gods and guests are served, intent upon the rites of the Veda, given to sacrifice and to giving, according to his means and according to the rule.

sanskrit: na pāṇipādacapalo na netracapalo muniḥ na ca vāgaṅgacapala iti śiṣṭasya gocaraḥ
english: The sage is not restless with hand or foot, not restless with the eye, nor restless in speech or limb—such is the proper sphere of the cultivated man.

sanskrit: nityayajñopavītī syāc chuklavāsāḥ śucivrataḥ niyato damadānābhyāṃ sadā śiṣṭaiś ca saṃviśet
english: He should always wear the sacred thread, be clad in white, of pure vows, restrained in self-control and giving, and should ever consort with the cultivated.

sanskrit: jitaśiśnodaro maitraḥ śiṣṭācārasamāhitaḥ vaiṇavīṃ dhārayed yaṣṭiṃ sodakaṃ ca kamaṇḍalum
english: Having mastered his loins and belly, friendly, settled in cultivated conduct, he should bear a staff of bamboo and a water-pot filled with water.

sanskrit: adhītyādhyāpanaṃ kuryāt tathā yajanayājane dānaṃ pratigrahaṃ caiva ṣaḍguṇāṃ vṛttim ācaret
english: Having studied, he should teach; likewise he should sacrifice and officiate at sacrifice, give and receive—thus he should follow the sixfold livelihood.

sanskrit: trīṇi karmāṇi yānīha brāhmaṇānāṃ tu jīvikā yājanādhyāpane cobhe śuddhāc cāpi pratigrahaḥ
english: Of these, three acts are the livelihood of brāhmaṇas: both officiating at sacrifice and teaching, and accepting gifts from a pure source.

sanskrit: avaśeṣāṇi cānyāni trīṇi karmāṇi yāni tu dānam adhyayanaṃ yajño dharmayuktāni tāni tu
english: And the other three acts that remain—giving, study, and sacrifice—those are bound up with sacred duty.

sanskrit: teṣv apramādaṃ kurvīta triṣu karmasu dharmavit dānto maitraḥ kṣamāyuktaḥ sarvabhūtasamo muniḥ
english: In those three acts the knower of duty should be vigilant: self-controlled, friendly, endowed with patience, a sage equal toward all beings.

sanskrit: sarvam etad yathāśakti vipro nirvartayañ śuciḥ evaṃ yukto jayet svargaṃ gṛhasthaḥ saṃśitavrataḥ
english: The pure brāhmaṇa, accomplishing all this according to his power—thus yoked, the householder of resolute vows shall win heaven.

sanskrit: brahmovāca evam etena mārgeṇa pūrvoktena yathāvidhi adhītavān yathāśakti tathaiva brahmacaryavān
english: Brahmā said: Thus, by this path declared before and according to rule, one who has studied to the best of his power and likewise observed celibacy—

sanskrit: svadharmanirato vidvān sarvendriyayato muniḥ guroḥ priyahite yuktaḥ satyadharmaparaḥ śuciḥ
english: the learned sage devoted to his own duty, restraining all his senses, intent on what is dear and good to his teacher, given to truth and righteousness, and pure—

sanskrit: guruṇā samanujñāto bhuñjītānnam akutsayan haviṣyabhaikṣyabhuk cāpi sthānāsanavihāravān
english: with his teacher's leave he should eat his food without disparaging it, living on sacrificial fare and on what is begged, regulated in standing, sitting, and movement.

sanskrit: dvikālam agniṃ juhvānaḥ śucir bhūtvā samāhitaḥ dhārayīta sadā daṇḍaṃ bailvaṃ pālāśam eva vā
english: Offering into the fire at the two times, having become pure and composed, he should ever bear a staff of bilva wood or of palāśa.

sanskrit: kṣaumaṃ kārpāsikaṃ vāpi mṛgājinam athāpi vā sarvaṃ kāṣāyaraktaṃ syād vāso vāpi dvijasya ha
english: The garment of the twice-born, whether of linen, of cotton, or even an antelope's hide, should all be dyed with ochre.

sanskrit: mekhalā ca bhaven mauñjī jaṭī nityodakas tathā yajñopavītī svādhyāyī aluptaniyatavrataḥ
english: His girdle should be of muñja grass; he should wear matted locks, perform his ablutions always, wear the sacred thread, study his lessons, and keep his fixed vows unbroken.

sanskrit: pūtābhiś ca tathaivādbhiḥ sadā daivatatarpaṇam bhāvena niyataḥ kurvan brahmacārī praśasyate
english: The celibate student who, restrained in his disposition, ever makes the offering of water to the gods with purified water, is praised.

sanskrit: evaṃ yukto jayet svargam ūrdhvaretāḥ samāhitaḥ na saṃsarati jātīṣu paramaṃ sthānam āśritaḥ
english: Thus yoked, with seed drawn upward and composed, he shall win heaven; he wanders no more among births, having reached the supreme abode.

sanskrit: saṃskṛtaḥ sarvasaṃskārais tathaiva brahmacaryavān grāmān niṣkramya cāraṇyaṃ muniḥ pravrajito vaset
english: Consecrated by all the sacraments and likewise observant of celibacy, the sage, departing from the villages and going forth into the forest, should dwell there.

sanskrit: carmavalkalasaṃvītaḥ svayaṃ prātar upaspṛśet araṇyagocaro nityaṃ na grāmaṃ praviśet punaḥ
english: Clad in hide and bark, at dawn he should himself perform his ablutions; ranging always in the forest, he should not enter a village again.

sanskrit: arcayann atithīn kāle dadyāc cāpi pratiśrayam phalapatrāvarair mūlaiḥ śyāmākena ca vartayan
english: Honoring guests in due season, he should also offer them shelter, sustaining himself on fruits, leaves, lowly roots, and wild millet.

sanskrit: pravṛttam udakaṃ vāyuṃ sarvaṃ vāneyam ā tṛṇāt prāśnīyād ānupūrvyeṇa yathādīkṣam atandritaḥ
english: He should partake, in due order and according to his consecration and unwearied, of flowing water, of air, and of all that the forest yields, down to grass.

sanskrit: āmūlaphalabhikṣābhir arced atithim āgatam yadbhakṣaḥ syāt tato dadyād bhikṣāṃ nityam atandritaḥ
english: With roots, fruits, and the alms he has gathered he should honor a guest who comes; whatever be his own food, from that he should ever give alms, unwearied.

sanskrit: devatātithipūrvaṃ ca sadā bhuñjīta vāgyataḥ askanditamanāś caiva laghvāśī devatāśrayaḥ
english: Serving the gods and guests first, he should always eat with restrained speech, his mind unwavering, eating lightly, his refuge in the gods.

sanskrit: dānto maitraḥ kṣamāyuktaḥ keśaśmaśru ca dhārayan juhvan svādhyāyaśīlaś ca satyadharmaparāyaṇaḥ
english: Self-controlled, friendly, endowed with patience, wearing his hair and beard, offering oblations, given to the study of scripture, and devoted to truth and righteousness—

sanskrit: tyaktadehaḥ sadā dakṣo vananityaḥ samāhitaḥ evaṃ yukto jayet svargaṃ vānaprastho jitendriyaḥ
english: having renounced care of the body, ever skillful, abiding in the forest and composed—thus yoked, the forest-dweller with senses subdued shall win heaven.

sanskrit: gṛhastho brahmacārī ca vānaprastho 'tha vā punaḥ ya icchen mokṣam āsthātum uttamāṃ vṛttim āśrayet
english: And the householder, the celibate student, or again the forest-dweller—whoever wishes to abide in liberation should take up the highest mode of life.

sanskrit: abhayaṃ sarvabhūtebhyo dattvā naiṣkarmyam ācaret sarvabhūtahito maitraḥ sarvendriyayato muniḥ
english: Having granted freedom from fear to all beings, he should practice freedom from action—the sage devoted to the welfare of all beings, friendly, restraining all his senses.

sanskrit: ayācitam asaṃkḷptam upapannaṃ yadṛcchayā joṣayeta sadā bhojyaṃ grāsam āgatam aspṛhaḥ
english: Unasked, unprepared for, and come by chance—such food he should always partake of, content with the mouthful that comes, free from longing.

sanskrit: yātrāmātraṃ ca bhuñjīta kevalaṃ prāṇayātrikam dharmalabdhaṃ tathāśnīyān na kāmam anuvartayet
english: He should eat only enough to sustain his journey, merely to keep life going; he should eat only what is righteously gained, and not pursue desire.

sanskrit: grāsād ācchādanāc cānyan na gṛhṇīyāt kathaṃ cana yāvad āhārayet tāvat pratigṛhṇīta nānyathā
english: Beyond a mouthful and a covering he should take nothing whatsoever; only as much as he may eat should he accept, and no more.

sanskrit: parebhyo na pratigrāhyaṃ na ca deyaṃ kadā cana dainyabhāvāc ca bhūtānāṃ saṃvibhajya sadā budhaḥ
english: He should accept nothing from others, nor ever give to them; but the wise one, out of compassion for the wretched state of beings, should always share what he has.
